title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Issuing the Final Invoice, Minimum Amount, Due Date and Closure
content:
## Clauses

**Minimum.** Should the detention and demurrage lines of a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record together fall short of the product's minimum invoice, the invoice is not sent and the record goes straight to settled.

**Invoicing deadline.** The product allows a set number of calendar days, reckoned from the day charges stopped accruing on the record, within which the final invoice has to go out.

- The clock for this deadline starts on the date charges stopped accruing, as recorded on the free-time record, never on a date the customer suggests.
- The last permitted day is found by stepping forward that many calendar dates from the stopping date.
- An invoice bearing the last permitted day's date is on time; one bearing any later date is late.
- If the last permitted day passes and no invoice has gone out, the charges have become uncollectible and the record is settled with no invoice at all.

**Record state.** A record takes invoice lines only while its status reads clock stopped or invoiced.

**Due date.** Payment is owed by the date reached by adding the product's payment term, in calendar days, to the invoice date; for a credit-approved customer whose credit days exceed that term, the credit days are added instead.

**Closure.** Once payments, waivers or credits have covered the invoice completely, the record is settled.

## Status changes on the record

| From | To | Occasion |
|---|---|---|
| clock stopped | invoiced | the final invoice is issued |
| clock stopped | settled | no day was chargeable, the total fell below the minimum, or the invoicing deadline passed with no invoice |
| invoiced | settled | payments, waivers and dispute credits have brought the balance due to 0.00 |

## Boundary cases on the deadline (hypothetical dates, with a deadline of 20 days assumed purely for illustration)

| Charges stopped accruing | Deadline day | Invoice dated | Judgement |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 April | 21 April | 21 April | in time |
| 1 April | 21 April | 22 April | late |
| 1 April | 21 April | 20 April | in time |

## Boundary cases on the minimum (hypothetical figures)

- A minimum of 40.00 and lines totalling 39.99: no invoice goes out and the record is settled.
- The same minimum and lines totalling exactly 40.00: the total is not below the minimum, so the invoice is raised.

## Due-date illustration (hypothetical)

An invoice dated 10 June on a product with an assumed 12-day term falls due on 22 June; for a credit-approved customer with 21 credit days it falls due on 1 July instead.
